dial.summary: TOTAL surged 5.85% to $2.87T on September 19 as the BOJ's +25bps hike the prior session weakened DXY to 100.21 and crypto decoupled from macro headwinds—BTC.D held firm at 56.68% and stablecoin dominance contracted to 10.67%, signaling net capital deployment into spot BTC; while real yields at 2.65% (18-year high) and DXY above 100 remain structural headwinds, the breadth of this rally (TOTAL +$150B in 24h, falling stablecoin share) and near-zero funding rates confirm BTC Accumulation conditions.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.5T as of September 2026 per MacroMicro/StreetStats (6–8 week lag means July is the last fully reported month); US M2 alone reached $23.2T in July 2026; 4-week trend up confirmed (sustained upward direction since mid-August); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); broader global M2 (all major central banks) at a record ~$150T as of mid-2026; BOJ's September 18 hike (+25bps to 1.25%) will modestly affect yen-denominated G4 components going forward but has no near-term impact on the reported aggregate.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; released Sep 1, below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down (Jul 55.6% → Aug 54.6% = −1.0pp); September ISM not released until October 1; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); S&P Global Flash PMI September 23 is the next advance read.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY closed at 100.2125 on September 18, 2026 (last trading day; September 19 is Saturday); DXY tested 5.04% 10Y equivalent pressure ahead of the FOMC Sep 16 hike, briefly touched 100.07 on Sep 17, then moderated to 100.21 on Sep 18 following the BOJ's +25bps hike to 1.25% (yen rallied to a 6.5-month high); 4-week trend up: Barchart confirmed DXY at ~99.60 on August 18, 2026 → 100.21 on Sep 18 = +0.61%, above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind (DXY above 100 threshold); the prior session's carry-trade unwind partially offset the FOMC-driven USD rally but DXY remains above the neutral band.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS reopening auction on September 17, 2026 cleared at a real yield of 2.653% — the highest for this term since October 2008 (per TipsWatch); FRED DFII10 secondary market was ~2.68% on September 16 per Federal Reserve H.15; using 2.65% as the auction-confirmed benchmark; 4-week trend up: ~2.45% (Aug 19 estimate) → 2.65% (Sep 17) = +20bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% threshold both met); elevated real yields remain the dominant macro drag on duration-sensitive and risk assets; sustainably falling below 2% required to shift status.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 18, 2026 close: 10Y ~4.94% (lost ~10bps after the BOJ hike from 5.04% FOMC-day peak), 2Y ~4.74% (per MacroRadar); spread = +0.20% (+20bps); 4-week trend down (flattening): ~+38bps (Aug 18, pre-FOMC) → +20bps (Sep 18) = −18bps, confirming sustained front-end repricing as 2Y anchored to elevated fed funds rate of 3.75%–4.00%; status neutral (positive spread but not steepening; supportive requires BOTH positive AND steepening; deeply inverted < −50bps for headwind does not apply); yield curve flattened further this week as the 10Y rally on BOJ yen strength compressed the spread.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,747B ($6.747T) for week ending September 16, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released September 17 (Treasuries $4,554B, MBS $1,914B, other $279B); next H.4.1 release scheduled September 24, 2026; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (Aug 13) → $6.747T (Sep 16) = +$47B, a modest expansion within the flat range; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no change to QT pace announced at Sep 16 FOMC; marginal expansion driven by FX swap line activity rather than new asset purchases).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate carried at +0.01% per 8h — Coinglass direct access unavailable due to network egress policy (value unchanged from prior run); TOTAL surged 5.85% to $2.87T on September 19 with BTC.D at 56.68%; near-zero funding on a +$150B 24h rally confirms spot-driven accumulation (not leveraged long build-up), consistent with BTC Accumulation conditions; status supportive (near-zero well below the 0.04% overheating threshold); if funding has risen with the rally, status could be at risk of shifting to neutral — to be confirmed when Coinglass data becomes accessible.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$306B (September 19, 2026; CoinGecko via search); total crypto market cap $2.87T (TOTAL surged 5.85% in 24h, BTC dominance 56.68%, BTC market cap $1.63T); stablecoin dominance 10.67% ($306B / $2.87T); 30-day trend down: from ~11.25% (Sep 18) and higher levels in August 2026 → 10.67% = clear 30-day declining trend as capital deployed from stablecoins into risk assets; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — rising dominance while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply as dominance fell while TOTAL surged); USDT leads at $183.4B (60.6%), USDC $74.2B; falling stablecoin dominance alongside rising BTC.D (56.68%) is the primary BTC Accumulation signal this cycle.

upcoming.title: S&P Global Flash PMI (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: S&P Global US Flash PMI Composite, Manufacturing, and Services preliminary data for September 2026 at 9:45 AM ET — first advance September activity read capturing the full post-FOMC (+25bps Sep 16), BOE hold (Sep 17), and BOJ hike (+25bps Sep 18) tightening reaction; leads ISM Manufacturing (Oct 1) and ISM Services; a sub-50 manufacturing reading would materially shift November FOMC rate-path narrative and reinforce TOTAL's recent decoupling from macro headwinds; consensus expects modest softening from prior reads.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 20, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 20, 2026 — labor market read in the first full week post-FOMC/BOE/BOJ tightening cluster; a sustained rise above 220K would signal early labor market cracks under fed funds rate of 3.75%–4.00%; prior weeks approximately 206K; labor resilience is key to the FOMC's case for sustained restrictive policy heading into October 27–28.

upcoming.title: Advance Durable Goods Orders (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Durable Goods Orders for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — watch non-defense capital goods ex-aircraft (key business investment proxy for Q3 GDP); elevated borrowing costs (10Y ~4.94%, real yields 2.65%) and DXY above 100 weigh on capex decisions; ISM Manufacturing new orders fell to 53.7 in August (−3.0pp); Q2 2026 GDP third estimate follows September 30.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Final)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers final September 2026 reading at 10:00 AM ET — first final sentiment read fully incorporating the post-FOMC (+25bps Sep 16), BOE hold (Sep 17), and BOJ hike (+25bps to 1.25%, Sep 18) trifecta; year-ahead inflation expectations closely watched; a sharp drop in current conditions or spike in inflation expectations could shift November FOMC positioning; released same day as Advance Durable Goods.
